requested_by: Rosa Delgado, Identity and Access Manager
title: Check this week's profile mappings, status changes and leaver offboarding in Okta
situation: Larkspur Example Co uses PeopleHub HR as the profile source for employees: HR data is imported into Okta, and Okta pushes profiles to Expense Portal and Team Chat. The help desk says some edits to users 'keep reverting', a few app profiles failed to update, and an admin has queued 11 status changes. Two people left this week: Marcus was deactivated and Ines was only suspended. Security wants proof, app by app, that neither can still get in.
your_task: Work out each of the 9 users' Okta profile and app profiles from the attribute mappings, and flag any mapping errors (missing source attribute, wrong data type, unknown source) and any edits that the source will overwrite.
Check each requested user status change against the Okta lifecycle and say whether it is allowed.
For each allowed change, say whether the user can sign in, whether sessions are cleared, whether app assignments are kept, and what happens to each app account.
Run the offboarding checklist for both leavers and mark every app ACCESS_REMOVED or STILL_HAS_ACCESS with the reason.
why_it_matters: If an attribute is owned by HR, fixing it in Okta only lasts until the next import, so the help desk keeps doing the same work. A wrong mapping can also give someone an approver flag they should not have. And a leaver who is only suspended, or whose app has no deprovisioning, can still get in: that is exactly what auditors and attackers look for.
done_when: All 9 users have a mapping outcome and computed profiles, with a reason for every error or overwritten edit.
All 11 status changes are marked ALLOWED or INVALID_TRANSITION, and allowed deactivations list each app account as DEACTIVATED, LEFT_ACTIVE_ORPHAN or NO_ACCOUNT.
Every offboarding check has an outcome, and each STILL_HAS_ACCESS has a named fix (deactivate instead of suspend, enable Deactivate Users, or disable the app account by hand).
The orphaned app accounts are listed for the app owners.

glossary.Profile source: The app or directory, here the HR system, that owns a user's profile; Okta imports from it, and its values win over edits made in Okta.
glossary.Profile Editor: The Okta Admin Console page where you see the Okta user profile, each app user profile, and the attribute mappings between them.
glossary.Attribute mapping: A rule that copies or transforms an attribute from one profile to another, for example from HR into Okta or from Okta into an app.
glossary.Okta Expression Language (EL): The small expression syntax used in mappings, such as String.toLowerCase(user.email).
glossary.Apply on create only: A mapping setting that fills a value once when the account is created and never updates it later.
glossary.Single sign-on (SSO): Signing in once with Okta and reaching apps without typing a separate password, using standards such as SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) or OIDC (OpenID Connect).
glossary.Secure Web Authentication (SWA): An Okta sign-in method where Okta stores the user's app username and password and fills them in; the app keeps its own password.
glossary.Deactivate Users: A provisioning feature that deactivates the user's account in an app when the user is deactivated in Okta.
glossary.Orphaned account: An app account that stays active after its owner has left or lost the Okta assignment.

talking_point: Checked attribute mappings for 9 users (4 OK, 2 edits overwritten by the source, 3 mapping errors such as text 'Yes' sent to a true/false field), validated 11 Okta status changes (7 allowed, 4 invalid, such as deleting a user who was not deactivated), found 3 app accounts left active as orphans after deactivation, and showed that 5 of 9 offboarding checks still had access, because a leaver was suspended instead of deactivated two apps accept their own passwords and one app was missing from the catalog.
